races.name: Randox Rated Hurdle

runners_data.name: Chanceawetmorning
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's 6yo has two wins from his last four starts and an excellent sim-going record of 2 wins and 4 places from similar Good conditions; sits prominently by nature and will look to track Trasna Na Pairce, with apprentice Josh Williamson claiming 5lbs a useful weight relief off 125.|
runners_data.comment: Chanceawetmorning brings strong recent form — a winner one start back and further wins three and four starts back — and has experience of today's trip and going; the main concern is a trainer operating at just 5% over the last fortnight.

runners_data.name: Cosmos d'Ainay
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy takes the ride for Elliott on this 6yo who won last time out and has a flawless six-run record on similar ground (2W 4P); his prominent style and recent winning form make him the standout tracking candidate, and his OR of 123 suggests he retains a degree of handicap scope.|
runners_data.comment: Cosmos d'Ainay is the one to beat here, winning last time out and again four starts back, with experience over today's trip and going working in his favour; a cool 30-day turnaround is ideal, though the trainer's current 5% strike rate is worth noting under 161 lb.

runners_data.name: Malbay Madness
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up operator with an excellent winning record on Good ground (4W 6P from 15 runs), but asks a straight question of how much pace the leader generates — the controlled tempo anticipated here means he may never get the strong gallop he needs to make up his ground from off the pace.|
runners_data.comment: Malbay Madness won back-to-back races before finishing eighth last time out, and with experience over today's trip and going he remains a lively threat — the key question is whether that latest below-par effort represents a blip or something more concerning.

runners_data.name: Trasna Na Pairce
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner in the field, Henry De Bromhead's 7yo wears a hood and has course-relevant Good-ground experience; form figures of 0-5274 suggest he is a generous pace-setter who doesn't always last home, but uncontested control here gives him every chance of lasting longer than his record implies.|
runners_data.comment: Trasna Na Pairce ran a solid second three starts back and returns fit on 18 days' rest, with experience of today's distance and going working in his favour; yet to win in recent starts, and the 159 lb burden is the key concern.

runners_data.name: Cap Bernat
runners_data.note: A 13yo returning from a 420-day absence for Robin McNeilly who has just one place from 10 runs on similar going; Danny Mullins's experience is the main asset, but the lengthy lay-off and age make it very hard to trust him in a competitive handicap hurdle.|

runners_data.name: Shinnhill
runners_data.note: Neil McKnight's 9yo is by nature a prominent racer but, with Chanceawetmorning, Cosmos d'Ainay, and Cap Bernat all likely to press for that position ahead of him, he is realistically likely to be pushed back into midfield and racing away from his comfort zone; his STYLE_FIT tag of 0.92 reflects a genuine positional risk, though he did win over 18f on Good ground in his recent history.|
runners_data.comment: Pulled up last time and off the track for 86 days, Shinnhill is hard to fancy on current evidence, ranked last on our figures; he has run over today's trip and going before, and that win three starts back is his sole recent bright spot.

runners_data.name: Tribal Moon
runners_data.note: A 5yo for amateur Ms E Dunseath (7lb claim) who ran just 8 days ago — quick turnaround warrants monitoring — and wears a tongue-pin; form figures of 0-730 and a sim-going record of 0 wins from 15 similar-ground runs make it very difficult to build a case, and the hold-up style requires a pace scenario that looks unlikely to materialise.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, with only a third two runs back to show for recent efforts, Tribal Moon faces a stiff task carrying 153 lb; he has run over today's going before, which offers some small comfort, but he remains hard to fancy ranked fifth of six on our figures.

races.paceDynamic: Trasna Na Pairce is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival to pressure them, Darragh O'Keeffe can dictate terms at whatever tempo suits, making this a strongly leader-biased setup on Good ground at Downpatrick. Chanceawetmorning, Cosmos d'Ainay, and Cap Bernat are all prominent-style horses who will want to sit just off the pace, creating a competitive pocket behind Trasna Na Pairce but unlikely to force a genuinely searching gallop from the front. Malbay Madness and Tribal Moon will be ridden from further back and will need the pace to quicken sufficiently to close ground in the straight. The field holds more prominent/front-running types than can all secure their natural berth — Shinnhill is the runner most likely to be shuffled back from their natural position, as Chanceawetmorning and Cosmos d'Ainay (better-credentialed Elliott runners) will dominate that prominent slot. This race shape — a single uncontested front-runner operating at a controlled pace over 2m2f on Good ground — strongly favours horses who can track the leader closely and strike from a handy position, giving the prominent horses behind Trasna Na Pairce the tactical advantage over true hold-up types.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Leader Controls, Prominent Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Trasna Na Pairce dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and the prominent horses track smoothly before challenging from 2 out.
scenarios.body: Trasna Na Pairce sets a sustainable fractions-controlled tempo and the race unfolds as a procession until the field begins to wind up approaching the final two hurdles; the horses sitting closest — Chanceawetmorning and Cosmos d'Ainay — are ideally positioned to challenge and overhaul a tiring leader. Prominent-style horses with strong form on Good ground benefit most from this predictable, rhythm-based shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Trasna Na Pairce jumps boldly, builds a decisive advantage early, and the prominent horses are unable to close the gap from 2 out.
scenarios.body: With no horse willing or able to pressurise Trasna Na Pairce at any stage, the leader is allowed to bowl along in their own time and conserves enough energy to repel late challengers; De Bromhead's runner, who has course form at Downpatrick and handles Good ground, becomes very hard to catch. This scenario suits horses with front-running ability who can measure their effort without the usual cost of having to fight for the lead.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Finish Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than anticipated — perhaps Cap Bernat or Chanceawetmorning push on to make a race of it — and the front end ties itself up in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: A contested early gallop causes the lead group to empty out before the last, leaving a gap for Malbay Madness to close from off the pace; however, Tribal Moon lacks the class and consistent form to capitalise, and Malbay Madness's Good-ground record (4 wins, 6 places from similar conditions) makes them the likeliest beneficiary of this shape. This scenario is discounted because no genuine second pace-maker exists to create the necessary breakneck fractions.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos Suits Outsiders
scenarios.trigger: If the field crawls at an unusually slow pace and the race degenerates into a sprint finish from the final hurdle, scrambling the form.
scenarios.body: A sprint-finish scenario removes the advantage of horses with superior stamina and class, theoretically giving an outsider like Shinnhill a narrow window — though Shinnhill is racing out of their natural prominent role and their STYLE_FIT tag tempers confidence significantly. Cap Bernat, a veteran with place form at this trip, might stay on one-paced to fill a frame position, but this scenario relies on an unlikely combination of slow pace and maximum positional disruption.

watchPoints.text: Trasna Na Pairce's jumping must be monitored from the outset — if they fluff an early hurdle and lose their uncontested lead, the entire race shape collapses and a prominent horse will inherit an even more straightforward task.

Cosmos d'Ainay and Chanceawetmorning are both prominent-style Elliott runners who will want the same position — watch the early battle for the prime tracking spot, as one may be shuffled wider or further back than ideal.

Cap Bernat is 420 days absent and 13 years old — if Danny Mullins sends him forward aggressively to compensate for the layoff, it could briefly complicate Trasna Na Pairce's rhythm before Cap Bernat fades.

Shinnhill's early positioning is worth tracking: if the prominent horses fill all the handy berths as expected, watch whether Patrick M O'Brien (5) drops him in or attempts to force a position, as his chance largely hinges on which shape he ends up in.

Tribal Moon's quick return (8 days) for a 7lb amateur claimer is worth flagging — if the horse shows any sign of reluctance or flat jumping under pressure, connections may have a specific target in mind and this run could be treated as prep rather than a genuine win attempt.

races.name: Lily O'Hare Memorial Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Kalsman
runners_data.note: An 8yo hold-up performer who has won over 20f on Good ground and placed in similar company; trainer Liam Lennon has a blank 14-day record but Kieren Buckley takes the ride, and 57 days off typically means a freshened horse — the chief closer to side with if the pace is genuine.
runners_data.comment: Kalsman was third last time out but a winner four starts back, and he does bring experience over today's trip and going. Fifty-seven days off the track raises a fitness query, and his 168 lb burden is a significant ask for a horse ranked fifth of twelve.

runners_data.name: Pralognan
runners_data.note: 255 days off is the single biggest concern here — A J Martin sends out a yard in form (2/11 over 14 days) but this 7yo's recent runs have been at shorter trips on varying ground and the layoff combined with step up in distance makes its stamina an open question.
runners_data.comment: Pralognan won three starts back and has experience of both today's trip and going, making him a clear danger — the chief concern is that 255 days off the track leaves his fitness an open question.

runners_data.name: Tropical Twist
runners_data.note: Only 2 days since last run is bold fresh usage by Gordon Elliott, and Jack Kennedy's presence signals confidence — this 5yo won over 17f on Good last time and its hold-up style should translate well to tracking Parkgarve into the straight, making it one of the most interesting pace-shape beneficiaries.
runners_data.comment: Tropical Twist arrives on the back of a win last time out and has experience of both today's trip and going, giving her solid claims here; the chief concern is a trainer firing at just 5% in recent weeks.

runners_data.name: Augusta George
runners_data.note: A genuine prominent racer whose second over 22f at Downpatrick-comparable Good ground reads well; W J Bryson's yard is 0/0 over 14 days and the 226-day absence is a flag, but the style fit for tracking Parkgarve is natural and the course trip profile is the strongest in the race.
runners_data.comment: A second three starts back highlights Augusta George's class, and he has experience over today's trip and going — our rating of 106 makes him the one to beat in this field. Yet to score in recent starts and a 226-day absence are the only reservations.

runners_data.name: Parkgarve
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner who sets the race's entire pace architecture; tagged with a STYLE_FIT discount because it is operating out of its natural element in terms of the field density, and its 0W record from 13 Good-ground runs suggests it gives way when tested, but it controls the tempo until then.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Parkgarve does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and 23 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh; the concern is a top weight of 159 lb, which gives his rivals a handy pull.

runners_data.name: Barrogstown Girl
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up type whose real position is from the rear — the map places her in midfield only because the race is overloaded with closers; her best run was a second over 19f on Good, and Aidan Kelly's mount will need a clean passage that the congested back half of this field may not provide.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Barrogstown Girl does bring distance and going experience to the table, but a run just two days ago raises obvious freshness concerns; second two starts back offers a glimmer, though her overall profile here leaves her with plenty to prove carrying 158 lb.

runners_data.name: Leitzel
runners_data.note: Six consecutive double-figure finishes across 12–20f distances on Good ground paint a grim picture; the 5lb claim of Alan O'Sullivan offers some compensation but this 6yo shows no indication of reversing its form decline in a competitive handicap.
runners_data.comment: Leitzel showed a flash of ability when finishing third five starts back, and she has experience of today's trip and conditions — but winless in her last five starts and returning after 97 days off, there are questions about whether that form has been maintained.

runners_data.name: Fine Print
runners_data.note: John C McConnell's 5yo has been freshened over 28 days and showed its best form when placed over 14f at Standstead; the horse carries headgear (hood/tongue-tie) and is a true hold-up type forced into midfield by field composition — shorter trips have suited better and 18f may stretch its range.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with an unplaced effort 28 days ago the latest in a patchy sequence, Fine Print faces a stiff task here. He has run over today's trip and going, but a trainer without a strike in 25 recent attempts and a ranking of ninth of twelve make him hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Granlahan
runners_data.note: Adrian McGuinness has been firing (2/26 over 14 days) and Darragh O'Keeffe is an upgrade in the saddle for this 4yo who has placed three times in five Good-ground runs; naturally a hold-up type displaced into midfield, but the consistent placing record gives it a better-than-average chance of running into a frame position if the pace materialises.
runners_data.comment: Consistent enough in places — third two starts back and third four starts back — but yet to win in recent starts and that sixth last time out is a concern; has run over today's trip and going, and 149 lb is no featherweight assignment for a gelding rated 83 officially.

runners_data.name: Gortmore Lady
runners_data.note: Carries headgear (hood/tongue-tie) and has placed over 18f on Good, but a four-run losing streak and a pulled-up run in the recent past tempers enthusiasm; her natural style is hold-up and she is squeezed into midfield on the map — the amateur rider Mr J Costello (7) faces a tough task getting a clean run from a crowded field.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts — including a pull-up and a brought-down — Gortmore Lady faces a stiff task carrying 148 lb, and her trainer is without a winner in 22 attempts over the past fortnight; experience over today's trip and going offers slim consolation.

runners_data.name: Mount Hotham
runners_data.note: Flagged as a horse that fades in the finish, with zero places from nine Good-or-similar-ground runs and consecutive single-digit finishes — Danny Mullins is a reliable jockey but even his partnership cannot mask a form profile that gives little cause for optimism over 18f.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Mount Hotham faces a stiff ask here; experience over today's trip and going counts in his favour, but his recent string of poor efforts makes him hard to fancy at the weights.

runners_data.name: La Rocca Lass
runners_data.note: Five consecutive zeros across all going types, flagged as fading in the finish, and the lightest-weighted runner in the field at 142lbs; Joshua Halford (7) takes the ride and the tongue-tie reappears, but the historical evidence — finishing 10th–15th repeatedly — offers no realistic hook for any scenario.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and back out just two days after her latest unplaced effort, La Rocca Lass faces a stiff task ranked 11 of 12 on our figures; experience on today's going is about the best that can be said for her.

races.paceDynamic: Parkgarve is the one confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner handicap hurdle over 2m2f at Downpatrick and, with no other genuine lead type to press it, is likely to control proceedings at a measured, sustainable gallop on Good ground. The pace dynamic is fundamentally straightforward: Parkgarve sets a tempo dictated by its own comfort rather than external pressure, which typically produces a race run at a fair but not scorching pace before the field compresses entering the final circuit. However, the field contains a significant cluster of true hold-up horses — Barrogstown Girl, Fine Print, Granlahan, Gortmore Lady, Mount Hotham and La Rocca Lass — who are mapped to midfield purely because there is no room at the rear given how many share that profile; none of them are likely to secure a genuinely wide-open prominent position, and that overcrowding in the midfield-to-rear section creates a messy tactical picture for late runners. Augusta George is the one horse with legitimate prominent credentials to challenge Parkgarve's position, and Kalsman and Tropical Twist are the most credible closers from hold-up ground. The tactical verdict favours horses who can travel prominently in behind Parkgarve at an uncontested pace — prominent-to-midfield types who track the leader into the straight are most advantaged, because the true hold-up horses face a congested, compromised trip and must produce a significant move from deep.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Parkgarve Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Parkgarve leads uncontested and Augusta George slots in second, setting a steady rhythm that stretches the field without quickening sharply.
scenarios.body: Parkgarve dictates on its own terms throughout, and the race becomes a test of stamina and jumping efficiency rather than late pace; prominent trackers who can match strides turning for home are best placed. Augusta George, with a course-applicable record and prominent style, is the profile that benefits most alongside any horse who travels fluidly in the top three.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely moderate and a horse sitting second or third conserves enough energy to cruise past Parkgarve at the last.
scenarios.body: A slow-to-moderate tempo from Parkgarve creates a steadily-run race where the winner comes from just off the shoulder of the leader in the final 2f; this shape rewards horses with tactical pace and jumping fluency over the final two hurdles. Tropical Twist, fresh from a recent win and ridden by Jack Kennedy, and Kalsman, who has shown the ability to hit the front from a hold-up position, are the profiles that capitalise.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Reel In Field
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens mid-race and the front two are set alight early, draining stamina reserves and allowing the back half to close.
scenarios.body: A faster-than-expected tempo would leave Parkgarve and Augusta George vulnerable in the final half-mile, opening the door for a horse who has been restrained and travels well through the field. Kalsman has form at this trip on Good ground and finished first over 20f on Good, while Granlahan's consistent placing record suggests it can sustain a late run — though both face the redistribution squeeze.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Favours Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If the crowded midfield causes interference, shuffled horses, or jumping errors that disrupt the fancied runners.
scenarios.body: With six or more horses jostling for identical ground from the rear to midfield, a rough passage or a faller in the pack could see an unconsidered runner emerge from the melee; Gortmore Lady has placed at this trip on Good and carries headgear, and Fine Print placed recently at a closely related distance. This is a low-probability scenario but the sheer density of hold-up types crammed together makes it non-trivial.

watchPoints.text: Tropical Twist ran just 2 days ago — monitor market moves and any jockey comment; if Elliott has backed up this horse so quickly it may have peaked, or alternatively it arrives cherry-ripe and Kennedy's confidence is the cue.

Augusta George has been off 226 days and is unproven returning from a long break — if it misses its stride in the early prominent position it could compromise the whole race shape by creating a gap that Parkgarve exploits freely.

The midfield is dangerously crowded with six true hold-up horses compressed into the same ground — watch for early interference, shuffled-away runners or a jumped-across moment at the second or third hurdle that eliminates a fancied closer before the race properly develops.

Parkgarve's 0W-from-13 record on Good ground is a persistent flag — if it capitulates turning for home rather than being passed cleanly, it risks causing a concertina behind it among the prominent and midfield horses who have been tracking closely.

Granlahan's trainer McGuinness is 2/26 over the past 14 days — a yard in form sending out a horse with multiple recent placings on Good ground is worth monitoring for a market move, particularly as Darragh O'Keeffe's booking adds further interest.

races.name: Franco Hughes Away Bet Mares Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Cobra Queen
runners_data.note: Strong sim-going record (14 from 15 on Good, 4 wins), headgear noted, held-up mare whose best trip appears to be around 2m2f-2m3f — the step to 2m6f is worth querying despite the De Bromhead/O'Keeffe combination.|
runners_data.comment: Cobra Queen bounced back to form with a third last time out after a couple of disappointing efforts, and she has experience over today's trip and going. Carrying 166 lb is a notable ask, but as the top-rated runner she appeals most.

runners_data.name: Samba Train
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner; won on Good at 2m2f last time, unseated the run before, and with only 8 career runs on Good ground this is a consistent profile — Walsh will dictate and the key question is whether the pace she sets is honest enough to stretch the field.|
runners_data.comment: Samba Train won two of her last five starts, with a victory two runs back highlighting her strong claims here, and she has experience of today's distance and going — the only question mark is that unseating last time out.

runners_data.name: Billie Frechette
runners_data.note: Amateur rider (7lb claim for Tegetmeier) on a mare who has placed twice at 2m2f Good but posted a 16th on last course visit — headgear (tongue-tie) noted and Meade sends runners in decent form, but the claim and the trip at 2m6f for the first time are angles to weigh.|
runners_data.comment: Twice a runner-up in recent starts and third two starts back, Billie Frechette arrives fit on just 11 days' rest, has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 122 marks her out as a genuine danger at the weights — though she remains winless and will need to convert that consistent placing form into a win.

runners_data.name: Theflyingbee
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with a 2nd on Good last time (2m, recent), 87 days off the track — trainer Hand has zero runners in the past 14 days which is a freshness flag; handles Good well (9 from 15) but steps up markedly in trip to 2m6f for the first time.|
runners_data.comment: Theflyingbee has been consistently placed, finishing second last time out and third in each of the two starts before that, and she has experience of today's trip and conditions — our rating of 126 marks her as a serious threat. The concern is 87 days off the track.

runners_data.name: Camlin Park
runners_data.note: Headgear (tongue-tie), won over 2m2f Good, but the P-P-P run pattern from recent starts raises jumping confidence concerns at a track like Downpatrick — went 7th last time after a lay-off so fitness improving, Good ground suits (3 from 5 on similar).|
runners_data.comment: Camlin Park won one start back from two pulled-up efforts and a seventh, so her form is patchy at best, and a trainer without a winner in 25 recent attempts is a concern; she has going experience in her favour, though 159 lb is a significant burden.

runners_data.name: Poetic Twist
runners_data.note: Elliott/Kennedy combination always commands respect; four seconds in her last five starts suggests she finds one too good rather than being found out — 2m6f is a new trip but her Good-ground consistency (4 from 6 with a win) and prominent style is ideally suited to following Samba Train.|
runners_data.comment: Poetic Twist won two starts back and has placed in four of her other last five outings, showing admirable consistency, but a 55-day break, a struggling trainer at 5% and a hefty 157 lb to carry are real negatives to weigh against her.

runners_data.name: Gangster Granny
runners_data.note: Two wins and a 2nd in three starts over 2m2f Good, last run 26 days ago — the hold-up style and course-distance form are the standout credentials here, and Flanagan is a shrewd handler of this type of mare in a moderate-pace handicap.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked ninth of eleven on our figures, Gangster Granny is hard to fancy at the weights, carrying 154 lb, though she arrives in decent heart — a winner last time out and a second two starts back — and has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Joya Del Mar
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old mare with wins over 2m2f Good, hold-up style, headgear (noted as p) — Patrick O'Brien's 5lb claim is relevant in a 12-runner handicap; form includes a 13th and a 6th in recent starts, suggesting inconsistency, and the drop to OR=106 may bring her back to her mark.|
runners_data.comment: Placed third last time out and a winner two starts back, Joya Del Mar brings solid recent form and has run over today's trip and going before, but she carries 154 lb and our rating ranks her eighth of eleven — a live each-way contender rather than a clear standout.

runners_data.name: Oh Janey
runners_data.note: Won over 2m2f Good, prominent style, headgear (tongue-tie), but last five starts show a 1W from positions that include a 6th and 6th recently — Crawford yard has zero 14-day runners and there is no strong freshness angle; will need a clean run from a prominent berth.|
runners_data.comment: A winner four starts back, but Oh Janey has posted three consecutive finishes out of the frame since, and 152 lb is a stiff burden to reverse that slide; she has run over today's trip and going before, at least lending some comfort.

runners_data.name: Shannon Bank
runners_data.note: Won over 2m flat on Good, but his natural hold-up style means he is placed in midfield here only because the rear is full — a true closer racing forward of his comfort zone, the 40-day absence and declining form string (7-1-7) make it hard to enthuse unless the race falls apart in front of him.|

runners_data.name: Miss Lia
runners_data.note: Won at 2m2f on soft, placed twice at 2m1f on soft/heavy, headgear (p) — her best form is on softer ground than today's Good, and being a genuine hold-up type squeezed into midfield by the field's composition compounds the challenge; 57 days off and OR=93 means she needs things to go perfectly.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked last on our figures, Miss Lia faces a stiff ask here; a 57-day absence and 141 lb add to her concerns, though she has run over today's trip and going before, and a second three starts back offers a faint crumb of comfort.

runners_data.name: Steps In The Sand
runners_data.note: Ran just 3 days ago which is an extreme turnaround — prominent style, amateur (7lb claim for Costello), OR=91 is the lowest in the field; recent form (4-3-4) is honest but uninspiring, and the quick reappearance after a race three days prior is the single biggest red flag in the race.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked tenth of eleven on our figures, Steps In The Sand faces a stiff task; a trainer without a return from 22 runners in the past fortnight is a further concern, though she has run over today's trip and going before.

races.paceDynamic: Samba Train is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger likely to press from the outset, Mark Walsh can control tempo from the front at a sustainable clip over this 2m6f trip on Good ground. Five runners want prominent positions — Theflyingbee, Camlin Park, Poetic Twist, Oh Janey, and Steps In The Sand — creating a congested bunch directly behind Samba Train from the first fence, and that cluster will generate friction and shuffling between the 2nd-last and last. The field contains more hold-up types than can genuinely settle at the rear: Shannon Bank and Miss Lia are true hold-up horses redistributed to midfield because Cobra Queen, Billie Frechette, Gangster Granny, and Joya Del Mar are all also sitting deep, meaning Shannon Bank and Miss Lia will likely have to race closer than they want. This race shape — a lone front-runner setting a measured pace with a prominent bunch in pursuit — classically favours a well-placed prominent racer who can travel smoothly behind Samba Train and strike turning in, rather than a deep hold-up horse who may find the prominent congestion seals the gaps late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Samba Train Controls, Prominent Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Samba Train dictates an uncontested, honest-but-not-blistering gallop and a prominent tracker delivers a clean jump two out.
scenarios.body: Samba Train bowls along at the front with the prominent pack — Poetic Twist, Theflyingbee, Camlin Park — tracking closely; the one who jumps cleanest at the second-last earns first run and the Good ground suits a front-to-back finish. Poetic Twist's consistency (four seconds in last five, won 2m2f Good) and Jack Kennedy's big-race sharpness make her the standout in this shape, with Theflyingbee's recent 2nd on Good also relevant.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Scrimmage, Hold-Up Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the five prominent horses crowd each other and cause interference between the final two hurdles, opening a lane for a hold-up mare to come through.
scenarios.body: With the mid-race bunch running into each other on the home turn, a horse held just off the pace but capable of switching gears benefits; Gangster Granny and Cobra Queen, both with genuine Good-ground hold-up credentials and strong sim-going records, are best placed to capitalise on a gap. Gangster Granny's two wins and a second over this exact course-and-distance profile on Good is the key form pointer here.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Samba Train Gallops Rivals Flat
scenarios.trigger: If Samba Train ups the tempo significantly on the final circuit and the race becomes a stamina test that exposes the lower-rated prominent types.
scenarios.body: A strongly-run 2m6f on Good ground favours horses with proven staying ability and a good jump at the last; Cobra Queen (won 2m2f Good, placed at 2m3f and 2m4f repeatedly) and Billie Frechette (consistent in staying trips) have the profiles to stay on best. Samba Train's own U last time out adds some doubt, but if Bolger sends her out to dominate, the race can be won from the front if rivals are cooked.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Suits Deep Closers
scenarios.trigger: If multiple fallers or unseated riders thin the field and create a truly muddling pace that rewards horses held back off all the trouble.
scenarios.body: Shannon Bank and Miss Lia — genuine hold-up types mapped into midfield due to congestion at the rear — would need this scenario to race in their true role and arrive late with a clean passage. Shannon Bank's two wins on Good at 2m and form placing at 2m1f suggests she can close, but the STYLE_FIT discount is real and this shape depends on a chaotic unfolding rather than design.

watchPoints.text: Steps In The Sand ran just three days ago — watch the pre-race inspection carefully and monitor whether the horse moves freely, as a horse at OR=91 turning around in 72 hours in a 12-runner hurdle over 2m6f is a significant welfare and performance risk.

Prominent congestion between Theflyingbee, Camlin Park, Poetic Twist, Oh Janey, and Steps In The Sand will be most acute at the first two hurdles — watch for scrimmaging that could bring down or badly hamper a mid-field hold-up horse in a chain reaction.

Samba Train unseated last time out (U in form string) — if Walsh has any issue settling her in front or she makes a jumping error at a critical hurdle, the entire race shape collapses and mid-field hold-up types are suddenly gifted a muddling pace they can exploit.

Camlin Park has a P-P-P jumping pattern in recent form — at Downpatrick, a sharp, right-handed, undulating track, a horse with confidence issues at hurdles is a material danger to any horse racing immediately behind it on the approach to the home straight.

Shannon Bank and Miss Lia — both genuine hold-up types mapped into midfield — will likely be closer to the pace than they want; watch whether either jockey chooses to drop them back deliberately to their natural rear position, which would be the tactically honest move but risks losing ground on a track that can front-run well.

races.name: J Murdoch Contracts Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: G N Jefferson
runners_data.note: Prominent-racing 5yo for McConnell who has shown a tendency to fade in the finish; Shane Fitzsimons (7) takes the ride, and all three turf runs on good ground are without a win or place, though a stalking role behind the sole front-runner here suits his style better than most of those efforts.|

runners_data.name: I Can Find Em
runners_data.note: Returned just 11 days ago and finished 0th of field on that outing; genuine hold-up horse by inclination but the density of closers in this field means Gary McGill's 5yo is likely to find itself racing more forward than ideal, and the STYLE_FIT flag of 0.90 tempers confidence accordingly.|

runners_data.name: Lygon Lad
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy takes over on Gordon Elliott's lightly-raced 6yo returning from a 490-day absence — that layoff is the dominant concern; by nature a hold-up horse, though in a field stacked with closers he will not get a clear last-to-first run, and his best form came at shorter distances on soft.|

runners_data.name: Paymelater
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old for Millar with a consistent recent record of mid-division finishes in the 0W2P bracket on good ground; a true hold-up style means he needs the pace to stack the field out over this stamina trip, and his 10/12 sim-going strikes without a win is a telling honesty check on his ceiling.|

runners_data.name: That's It Paddy
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the race; Conor Stone-Walsh can slot him straight to the front and dictate terms entirely unchallenged, and on good ground over 2m6f an uncontested leader who jumps cleanly is a potent tactical asset even with modest form (4P-6).|

runners_data.name: Young Doran
runners_data.note: Ran only once, finishing second over 2m2f on good ground, and arrives here with the freshness of 76 days off; Tiernan Power Roche rides for Rothwell, and the step up to 2m6f looks like it will suit this hold-up type if he can get a true-run race behind a front-runner who goes hard enough.|

runners_data.name: Magical Sal
runners_data.note: Consistent form figures including a recent second on good ground for Slevin and McBratney; a natural hold-up horse wearing a hood, but with several other closers in the field she is mapped forward of her comfort zone, and the 0.93 STYLE_FIT reflects that her finishing kick may not be triggered in a slow-run race.|

runners_data.name: Thesilverbridle
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and flagged as such, but posted a second over 2m on good ground last time for McConnell; style is uncertain (U) which in this context may be an asset — Kenneally (5) can position him wherever the race dictates, and a clean-jumping, adaptable sort could slot in just behind That's It Paddy and prove dangerous.|

runners_data.name: Oops A Daisy
runners_data.note: Four-year-old hurdler for Hanlon and Younge (7) with three runs all producing finishes of 7th, 11th, 11th — consistent non-competitiveness on good ground; a hold-up style who fades in the finish is the hardest profile to win from in an uncontested pace scenario, and the lightest weight (147lbs) does not obviously change that.|

races.paceDynamic: That's It Paddy is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 9-runner maiden hurdle over 2m6f at Downpatrick, and with no obvious challenger for the lead, Conor Stone-Walsh can dictate terms at whatever tempo suits, making this an uncontested lead scenario on good ground. The strong hold-up contingent — Paymelater, Young Doran, Oops A Daisy — will be forced to settle well off the pace, creating a clear divide between a lone leader and a chasing pack that must deliver their effort late over this stamina-testing trip. This field contains more hold-up types than the pace map can place at the rear: Magical Sal, I Can Find Em, and Lygon Lad are genuine hold-up horses redistributed into midfield positions they are unlikely to naturally occupy, meaning the race will likely compress into a lead-and-chase dynamic rather than a true multi-layer finish. The race shape strongly favours prominent or patient-tracking profiles who can stalk That's It Paddy through the middle section and pick up when he ties up — true deep closers face a harder task if the pace is controlled and the winner dictates a steady gallop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Controls
scenarios.trigger: If That's It Paddy bowls along unchallenged and sets a fair-to-steady gallop that irons out the field behind him.
scenarios.body: That's It Paddy controls every yard from the front, and a horse that has been tracking him through the middle miles swoops to lead at the last or on the run-in; the 2m6f trip on good ground rewards a measured early pace and a clean jump at every hurdle.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a prominent-to-midfield horse tracks That's It Paddy closely and strikes for home after the second-last hurdle.
scenarios.body: G N Jefferson or Thesilverbridle sit within two lengths of the leader throughout and produce a clean jump at the penultimate hurdle to go clear; this shape rewards horses with a P or stalking profile who handle good ground and get the extra distance.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Hold-Up Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is hot enough early to string the field out and genuine closers get a true-run race over the full 2m6f trip.
scenarios.body: Paymelater or Young Doran are produced with a sustained run from two out, picking off a tiring leader in the final 150 yards; this scenario requires That's It Paddy to have gone hard enough to flatten the midfield runners, which is possible but against the grain of his uncontested position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Scrambled Finish
scenarios.trigger: If That's It Paddy makes a critical jumping error or capitulates early, triggering a chaotic reshuffle.
scenarios.body: The race loses its structure and multiple horses hit the front at different points between three out and the last, creating a messy sprint finish where fortune and jumping accuracy decide the outcome.

watchPoints.text: That's It Paddy's jumping must be tracked from the outset — if he makes an early error under Conor Stone-Walsh the entire race shape collapses and the field is thrown open to whoever best handles the sudden acceleration.

Jack Kennedy on Lygon Lad is a major jockey upgrade on a 490-day returner for Gordon Elliott — watch in the betting and at the start for signs of racecourse freshness; Kennedy's ability to manufacture a run from an unpromising position is a real wildcard.

Magical Sal, I Can Find Em, and Lygon Lad are all natural hold-up horses competing for the same limited space at the rear — watch for crowding and interference on the first circuit as they negotiate their positions.

Young Doran's lone run returned a second over 2m2f on good ground; watch how Tiernan Power Roche positions him in the early stages — if he tracks the leader closer than expected, the step to 2m6f could make him a stayer who has been underestimated on limited evidence.

G N Jefferson and Thesilverbridle share the same trainer (McConnell) and ran just 16 and 17 days ago respectively — watch for any stable market drift or support as an indicator of which of the two McConnell runners the yard prefers in this contest.

races.name: Join Us For Ladies Day Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Ocean Of Dreams
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse whose sim-going record at Good (9 runs, 0W2P) is modest, and a recent string of poor finishes (14th, 8th, 6th) makes it hard to fancy at OR 94; Mr O McGill (5) is an amateur and this trip is longer than most recent starts.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked seventh of eleven on our rating, Ocean Of Dreams faces a stiff task under 166 lb; he has at least shown consistency in getting to the track, returning just 11 days after his latest eighth.

runners_data.name: Georgia Celena
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner and likely to control the pace entirely; Good-ground form is strong (sim-going 14/15, 1W6P) and John McConnell's yard is 0/25 in the 14-day window but the horse's tactical advantage here is real despite the style-fit note (0.93).
runners_data.comment: Georgia Celena arrives here just 17 days after finishing second, fit and in form, and she has run over today's trip and going before. Yet to land a race in recent starts, and her trainer is without a winner in the last fortnight, though her placed profile and conditions make her our pick.

runners_data.name: Speakasyoufind
runners_data.note: Hold-up type flagged for fading in the finish, which is a meaningful concern over 2m6f at Good; P J Rothwell yard in form (1/19 T14) and the horse has placed at Good ground, but the fade flag and OR 90 weight make it a risky each-way proposition.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, though that second two runs back offers some encouragement; he has run on today's going before and returns after 24 days, but 162 lb is a stiff burden for a horse ranked sixth of eleven.

runners_data.name: My Good Pal
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a solid sim-going record (10/15, 1W4P) and a win at 2m4f/Good on recent evidence; Gavin Cromwell sends him out fresh (16 days) and the tp headgear suggests he is likely to race with intent — well-suited to sitting just off a lone front-runner.
runners_data.comment: Fifth last time out and yet to win in his last five starts, My Good Pal does have distance and going experience in his favour and returns on a fresh 16 days; the main concern is connections' current 3% strike-rate, and 160 lb is a sizeable burden.

runners_data.name: Sneddy Eddie
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a frustrating recent record (4th, 5th, 5th, 13th, 26th) and no wins in sim-going (0W0P from 7 runs); Jack Kennedy is a quality booking but the horse's consistency issues at this level make it hard to advocate strongly.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked eighth of eleven on our ratings, Sneddy Eddie faces an uphill task carrying 157 lb, and a trainer firing at just 5% recently offers little encouragement; he has run over today's going before, though fourth last time out hints at some residual spark.

runners_data.name: Hay Baby
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse whose natural rear position is squeezed out by the weight of hold-up types in this field — the style-fit tag (0.91) reflects that it will not settle where it wants; Emmet Mullins yard in decent form (2/20 T14) but 0W0P in sim-going across 5 runs is a red flag.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Hay Baby nonetheless catches the eye on going and distance experience, and her rating of 88 suggests she's ahead of her official mark — though those back-to-back unplaced efforts are the concern she must overcome.

runners_data.name: Ballinagaine Girl
runners_data.note: Fade-in-finish flag combined with a redistribution away from her natural position at the rear; Danny Mullins is an excellent rider who may get more out of her than the style-fit (0.92) suggests, but 0W0P in Good-ground sim-going and an 11th on her last similar run dims the appeal.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with only a single second-place finish offering any encouragement, Ballinagaine Girl is also weighted at 155 lb and ranks a remote 10th of 11 on our figures — going experience is the one genuine positive.

runners_data.name: Bob The Builder
runners_data.note: Aged nine, fade-in-finish flag, and a redistribution note — Bob The Builder's best efforts have come at shorter trips and his 20th-of-20 at 2m1f/Good recently is alarming; P J Rothwell also trains Speakasyoufind, and between the two this one looks the lesser prospect.
runners_data.comment: Rated 93 and ranked top of this field, Bob The Builder arrives in solid fitness 30 days since his last start and has experience of today's going; winless in his last five, though, the concern is whether he can finally convert that improvement into something tangible.

runners_data.name: Something Simple
runners_data.note: Placed fourth at 2m2f/Soft and has shown some ability, but a string of pulled-ups (PPP) in the form figures and a style-fit discount (0.90) for being pushed out of natural position temper enthusiasm; Darragh O'Keeffe is a reliable jockey but 0W0P in sim-going is the story here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and twice pulled up in that sequence, Something Simple arrives here with obvious questions to answer; he has run over today's trip and going before, and our rating of 87 suggests some latent ability, but 151 lb is a stern burden for a horse so out of form.

runners_data.name: Sonna Lady
runners_data.note: Youngest runner in the field at four, only three career runs (all at Good), and 0W0P in sim-going — Conor Stone-Walsh takes the ride for a Hanlon yard that has had runners recently, but Sonna Lady's fade flag and step up to 2m6f look demanding at this stage of her career.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and ranked last on our figures, Sonna Lady faces a stiff ask carrying 148 lb, though she has run over today's going before and returns on a reasonable 23-day break.

runners_data.name: Sineads Fancy
runners_data.note: Natural prominent racer with a place record in sim-going (13/15, 1W3P) and consistent form at distances around 2m2f-2m6f/Good; Daniel King rides and S Ryan's small yard (T14:0/1) is quiet, but Sineads Fancy's ability to track Georgia Celena from a handy berth makes her one of the few who genuinely suits the likely race shape.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with a pulled up among the recent lowlights, Sineads Fancy faces a stiff ask ranked ninth of eleven on our figures; she has experience of today's trip and going, and 19 days between runs suggests she arrives fresh.

races.paceDynamic: Georgia Celena is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner 2m6f handicap hurdle and, with no other natural leader to press her, she is likely to control proceedings from the front at a pace she can sustain. The bulk of this field — Hay Baby, Ballinagaine Girl, Bob The Builder, Something Simple, and Sonna Lady — are genuine hold-up types who are compressed into midfield on the map simply because there is no room for them all at the rear; the horses most likely to actually secure the prominent positions behind Georgia Celena are My Good Pal and Sineads Fancy, who are natural prominent racers. With only one genuine pace-setter and a steady Good-ground gallop over 2m6f, this race shape strongly favours prominent and handy types who can track the leader without expending energy and produce a sustained run from two out — Georgia Celena herself cannot be dismissed, but horses who sit second or third on a controlled tempo and grind through the finish are best-positioned tactically.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Tempo, Front-Runner Stays
scenarios.trigger: If Georgia Celena dictates at a sustainable gallop and the hold-up pack fails to close in the final two hurdles.
scenarios.body: Georgia Celena sets a steady pace that suits her stamina, and with no serious challenger harrying her early, she conserves enough to hold on up the straight; her Good-ground record (14/15 sim-going entries) and prominent style make her the natural beneficiary of an uncontested lead.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Georgia Celena's lead is reeled in by a prominent tracker who has sat second or third throughout and produces a stronger finish.
scenarios.body: My Good Pal or Sineads Fancy, travelling comfortably just off the pace, benefit from the lack of early pressure and hit the front from the last hurdle with a fresher finish; this trip and Good ground suit My Good Pal who has placed at 2m4f/Good before.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closer Finds Gap
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough to string the field out and a genuine hold-up type threads through beaten horses to finish with purpose.
scenarios.body: Ocean Of Dreams or Speakasyoufind, dropping back into their natural rear-of-field position, pick off tired rivals in the closing stages if the tempo has been stronger than expected; Speakasyoufind's fade flag is a concern, but Ocean Of Dreams has placed at this going type and distance range.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Ridden Horses Rally
scenarios.trigger: If Georgia Celena goes too slow, the race bunches dramatically and hold-up types redistributed to midfield can produce an uncharacteristic late run.
scenarios.body: In a slowly-run race that becomes a sprint from the last, natural hold-up runners like Hay Baby or Ballinagaine Girl struggle to overcome both their style-fit penalty and their fade-in-finish flags; this scenario is unlikely precisely because those horses are not true hold-up types in this context and carry material style-fit discounts.

watchPoints.text: Georgia Celena is the only horse guaranteed to lead — watch whether My Good Pal or Sineads Fancy push up to challenge her before the final circuit, as any unexpected pressure could compromise her stamina.

Hay Baby, Ballinagaine Girl, Bob The Builder, Something Simple, and Sonna Lady are all true hold-up types who are unlikely to get their natural position — if they are forced to race more prominently than usual, watch for them to fade from two out.

Speakasyoufind carries a fade-in-finish flag and is a hold-up type in a race with only one confirmed pace-maker — if the pace is slow, the race will not set up for a late rattle and Speakasyoufind's chance is significantly diminished.

Jack Kennedy on Sneddy Eddie is the most high-profile jockey booking in the field; watch whether Elliott's runner is asked to move through from hold-up to midfield early, which would represent a change of tactics worth tracking.

Three horses from the John Joseph Hanlon yard run (Ballinagaine Girl, Something Simple, Sonna Lady) — watch for any signs of stable confidence through market moves, as a yard running three in one race sometimes has a preferred runner that betting patterns reveal.

runners_data.name: Greenmeansgo
runners_data.comment: Greenmeansgo makes his debut here carrying 168 lb — entirely unexposed and open to any amount of improvement, he's a fascinating unknown quantity on first appearance.

runners_data.name: Martymill
runners_data.comment: Martymill showed his best when second two starts back, and with experience over today's trip and going, the top-rated runner here looks the one to beat off 168 lb — though he remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Tommy's Ticket
runners_data.comment: Tommy's Ticket arrives here in good order on 19 days' rest, with going experience in his favour and a rating of 92 that marks him out as a genuine threat in this field; the concern is he's winless in his last two starts, and the hefty 168 lb burden may test him.

runners_data.name: Vargas
runners_data.comment: Vargas arrives after two consecutive pulls-up and a 245-day absence, with the trainer running at just 5% over the past fortnight; unexposed and lightly raced, he remains open to improvement, but there is plenty to prove under a hefty 168 lb.

runners_data.name: Culldoo
runners_data.comment: Unexposed after just the one start — a third last time out — Culldoo returns after 93 days with a trainer firing at 27% in the last 14 days and has scope for better with experience, though she carries a hefty 158 lb.

runners_data.name: Loves A Laugh
runners_data.comment: Loves A Laugh shaped well when third last time out, has run over today's trip and going, and returns on a fresh 26-day break with experience to draw on; the weight burden of 158 lb is the one factor to overcome.
